title: Persisted Queries
description: Use persisted queries to improve performance and security.

data.text: Persisted queries (also called automatic persisted queries or APQ) let clients send a hash of the query instead of the full query text. The server looks up the query by hash, saving bandwidth and enabling query whitelisting.
The client sends a SHA-256 hash of the query. If the server has seen it, it executes from cache. If not, the client sends the full query, and the server stores it.

data.caption: Persisted query flow.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    Client->>Server: Send query hash
    alt Hash exists
        Server-->>Client: Execute cached query
    else Hash missing
        Client->>Server: Send full query
        Server->>Server: Store by hash
        Server-->>Client: Execute and return result
    end

data.text: Hot Chocolate supports persisted queries through the `AddDefaultQueryStorage` and client-side libraries.

data.title: Server Setup

data.text: Use a GraphQL client that supports APQ, like Apollo Client or Relay. The client computes the hash and sends it automatically.

data.title: Apollo Client
Security Benefit
data.text: Persisted queries also act as a whitelist. Only queries that exist on the server can be executed, preventing malicious or accidental expensive queries.

terms.definition: A query stored on the server and referenced by its hash.
Automatic Persisted Queries — the protocol where clients send hashes and the server stores unknown queries.
A list of allowed queries, enforced by persisted queries.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Hashes let the server cache and lookup queries
APQ auto-stores new queries on first use
Persisted queries act as a security whitelist
